economicsExperiment.question: Historical model: how would uploader storage/egress obligations vary with retrieval count after a future purchase?
economicsExperiment.headline: STRUCTURALLY YES for ANT/AR on the uploader side (one-time prepaid; network serves retrievals) — but TWO PROOFS are required and NEITHER is done: (1) archive retrieved+restored from storage, (2) family experience delivered WITHOUT our box carrying the payload. Until (2), our estate-operated serving (box/relay) scales egress with every view.

arSplitRouteAnalysis.question: Is Arweave better used for the compact permanent provenance/root manifest while ANT carries the archive payload?
arSplitRouteAnalysis.finding: BOTH are within pocket change at this archive's size; the split becomes meaningful at scale (a 60 GB archive would cost ~$1,966 on AR vs a ~$0.09 manifest root + ANT payload at its own rate). Recommendation: quote BOTH routes at upload time and decide with live numbers; AR's manifest-root pattern (permanent, tiny, address-stable) pairs naturally with ANT's payload economics — but no duplication happens until both live quotes exist and the founder rules.
arSplitRouteAnalysis.scope: Historical pkg3 size/prices and hypothetical scaling only; superseded for the current edition by the exact-artifact quotes above.
